# Every netlink.LinkAdd in pkg/ and the parent-interface gate that
# covers it (#571).
#
# WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR
#
# A parent NIC registers one rx_handler, so it is a macvlan port or an
# ipvlan port and never both. Any child link attached to a parent must
# therefore be serialised against every other operation on that parent,
# which is what Plugin.lockParent does. A LinkAdd that reaches a parent
# without holding that gate can be refused with "device or resource
# busy" — surfacing to a user as a failed `docker run` caused by an
# unrelated container.
#
# WHAT THIS FILE DOES AND DOES NOT PROVE
#
# It does NOT prove the gate is held. Three of the sites below are
# gated by a CALLER, and proving reachability from a caller needs a
# call-graph analysis, not a text search. What this file proves is that
# every LinkAdd has been ACCOUNTED FOR: scripts/check-parent-gate-
# accounting.sh matches every netlink.LinkAdd in pkg/ and fails if any
# file is unlisted or its count has changed.
#
# So it catches the failure that actually happens — a new LinkAdd
# appearing on a parent with nobody having thought about the gate — and
# it does not catch someone deleting a lockParent call from a site
# already listed here. That gap is deliberate and recorded in #571.
#
# FORMAT
#
#   <path> <count>
#       <justification, indented, one or more lines>
#
# Entries are separated by blank lines. A bare path with no
# justification fails the gate: a list of paths with no reasons becomes
# a list somebody appends to. Same rule as .github/vuln-allowlist.txt.

pkg/plugin/parent_attached.go 1
    The endpoint's own child link, created during CreateEndpoint.
    Gated inline: lockParent is taken in the same function, immediately
    around the LinkAdd, and released as soon as it returns. The hold is
    deliberately short — an endpoint's link creation is microseconds and
    holding beyond it would serialise unrelated work.

pkg/plugin/orphan_release.go 2
    The reclaim's temporary dh-rel-* link, created to hand an orphaned
    lease back.
    Gated by the CALLER, several frames up, for the whole reclaim.
    DO NOT "TIDY" THIS INTO A LEXICAL LOCK AROUND THE LinkAdd. The hold
    must span the entire reclaim — the DHCP round trip AND the deferred
    LinkDel — because the parent stays occupied until that child link is
    gone, not merely until the DHCPRELEASE is sent. Shortening it to the
    LinkAdd restores the exact bug the gate was added for: an ipvlan
    reclaim link left on the parent while a macvlan endpoint is created,
    which is EBUSY on an operation the user did not cause.
    This is the entry a future reader is most likely to change, because
    making it lexical looks like an improvement.

pkg/plugin/dhcp_probe.go 1
    The validate_dhcp preflight probe's temporary link, created at
    network creation to prove a DHCP server answers on the parent.
    Gated by the CALLER in network.go, around the whole runDHCPProbe
    call. Lexical placement would be tidier and buys nothing under an
    accounting gate, so it is deliberately left alone rather than
    refactored inside a release (v1.7.0 follow-up).

pkg/plugin/network.go 1
    The bridge-mode veth pair. NOT a parent-attached child link: bridge
    networks have no parent NIC, nothing registers an rx_handler, and
    there is no parent to contend for. Correctly ungated, and adding a
    gate here would serialise bridge endpoints against nothing.
